Server-controlled allowlists (profiles, Bedrock endpoints, local endpoint approvals, env references) are checked on top and are not expressible here.

RawLine accepts object or positional struct array; stored canonical lines are separate. The externally tagged unit Meter accepts a name string or a single-key object whose value is null; responses always use strings. sku_label is non-blank text without control characters (C0, DEL or C1) of at most 80 CHARACTERS (label_valid counts chars(), not bytes, so maxLength is exact). The sku_label pattern's \s is ECMA-262 whitespace, which counts U+FEFF but not U+0085; the handler trims with Rust's Unicode White_Space, which counts U+0085 (also a C1 control, refused anyway) but not U+FEFF, so a value made only of U+FEFF is blank to an ECMA validator and not blank to the handler.

SetupDraftPriceLine.description: Exactly what the mapper emits (suggestion.rs map): not-applicable and explicit-unknown lines carry only their flag; priced lines carry no null placeholders. Prompt-size tiers exist only on the six token meters (overrides) and variants only on image lines. Audio meters price per minute or per hour only (the per-second batch can never be the first exact one because an exact per-second micro-USD amount is always exact per minute), search units are never priced by a catalog (rerank leaves them unknown), and realtime audio-token and video meters are never drafted.

The overflow rules (v3::bound) are on the price. The batch list must state exactly the meters of price_lines (same_meters): the same (meter, variant, min_prompt_tokens, not_applicable) keys and the same explicitly unknown meters, so it cannot add, drop or change the kind of a line; rates and amounts may differ. A mismatch is refused with 400; the schema compares no two properties, so it cannot express this. The batch list is bounded like price_lines.

oneOf.description: Version 1 (default): input and output rates, no cache pricing and no price lines. Version 2: additionally cache_pricing. Version 3: price_lines (and optional batch_price_lines/max_units), no rates and no cache_pricing. An input_token_limit of 0 is accepted only for a version 3 price whose input-family token meters are all not applicable (handler rule not expressible here). Version 1 and 2 take input_token_limit of at least 1 (validate_price: a zero input ceiling is only for version 3 prices whose input-family token meters are all not applicable). Charge arithmetic (validate_price; billing::charge(tokens, rate) = ceil(tokens x rate / 1000000)): every charge must fit a signed 64-bit integer and so must their sum. Version 1 charges input_token_limit at the input rate and output_token_limit at the output rate (each charge, then their sum). Version 2 (bound_v2) charges the same two amounts and, for every cache rate that is priced, charge(input_token_limit, cache rate): the input charge, the output charge and each cache charge (cache rate x input ceiling) must fit, and so must the total. Version 3 (v3::bound) charges per meter the highest applicable tier of ceil(ceiling x rate / batch), with input_token_limit as the ceiling of the input-family token meters, output_token_limit for output_tokens and the max_units entry for every other meter (a not_applicable meter, a zero ceiling and a missing line or max_units entry charge nothing); each such charge must fit and so must the sum over meters, and batch_price_lines is bounded the same way. The schema cannot multiply, so a rate and ceiling combination that overflows is refused by the handler (400) although each value is within its own bounds. Meter completeness (price_meters_incomplete, stored state): a version 3 price must state, as priced, not_applicable or unknown, every meter its route's workload can use (governance::price_meters: all twelve for chat, responses, messages, embeddings and rerank routes, fewer for image, transcription, speech, realtime and video routes; the workload follows the model's first supported protocol). Otherwise the handler answers 400 with reason price_meters_incomplete and the missing meter names in missing_meters; the schema cannot know the route.

SetupPolicy.description: Closed serde object or existing positional struct array in declared field order. Handler semantic validation is additional. nullable rate fields are required even when null. Supplied fields (jobs, storage, issuance, monthly budget): omission retains, null clears subject to tighten-only validation. Present fields (budget_period, budgets): omission is accepted but explicit null is rejected. The handler requires exactly one budget representation: the object form is a oneOf of the two forms (budgets, or monthly_budget_microusd with an optional budget_period). Positional form: serde accepts 3 to 10 elements, but the handler needs exactly one budget form (monthly_budget_microusd at index 7, optionally with budget_period at index 8, or budgets, never both), and a positional array cannot carry budgets without monthly_budget_microusd; only arrays of 8 or 9 elements reach a valid budget form (shorter ones carry none and a 10-element one carries both: the handler answers 400), so the contract's positional arm is exactly those two lengths and has no budgets item.

SetupVisibleBudgetWindow.description: A visible window whose accounting was read: every consumption fact is a value. remaining_microusd is null exactly when unknown_cost_requests is positive (budget_windows: remaining() needs zero unknown-cost requests). The facts are coupled (budget_windows): while unknown_cost_requests is 0 the headroom is known and remaining_microusd is a value; otherwise the headroom is unknown and remaining_microusd is null.

SetupWorkspacePolicy.description: Distinct visible/restricted projections: non-admin members can read limits, never workspace-wide storage/budget consumption.
